title: Uncontracted cartesian comparison of ordinary blowup towers
statement: Let $X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $h:Y\to X$ a morphism, and $A_0,\ldots,A_n$ and $B_0,\ldots,B_m$ ordinary blowup towers over $X$ and $Y$, with center ideals $I_i$ for $0\leq i<n$ and $J_i$ for $0\leq i<m$ [def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule]. An uncontracted cartesian comparison from $B$ to $A$ over $h$ consists of an equality $m=n$ and maps $b_i:B_i\to A_i$ for every $0\leq i\leq n$ (using that equality to identify index sets). For every $i$, the square with horizontal maps $b_i,h$ and vertical maps $B_i\to Y,A_i\to X$ is a fibre-product square [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every $0\leq i<n$, the maps commute with the adjacent tower transitions: $b_i\circ(B_{i+1}\to B_i)=(A_{i+1}\to A_i)\circ b_{i+1}$. Moreover $J_i=I_i\mathcal O_{B_i}$ is the full extended ideal along $b_i$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal]. Every stage, including every unit-ideal (empty-center) stage, is retained. No flatness assumption on $h$ is part of this definition; it specifies comparison data when those data exist.

source.place: VIII 2.1.7--2.1.9, printed pp.87--88: naive scheme-theoretic pullback of a blowup tower with its centers, without contraction.
